title: first100-flake-registry
description: Maintainer decision BLOCKED-007 item 3 (2026-09-01), evidence standard extended by BLOCKED-023 (2026-09-02): an append-only registry of tests confirmed flaky in this CI environment, independent of any First-100 slice's own changes. When a CI run's failing-test set is a subset of this registry's entries, that run's observation is a VALID observation for every other test in it -- no rerun needed for that reason alone (generate-ledger.mjs's checkObservationAgainstFlakeRegistry()). The registry never exempts a registered test from the suite itself: it still runs, still appears in the failure set, and a failure genuinely caused by the change under observation is never absorbed by this mechanism. Every entry must satisfy one of two evidence standards, mechanically verified by scripts/first100/verify-flake-registry.ts (not just asserted in the note): (a) >=2 occurrences on >=2 distinct candidateSha values (cross-SHA reproduction), or (b) >=2 occurrences on the SAME candidateSha with genuine outcome divergence -- at least one occurrence recorded 'failed' and at least one recorded 'passed' for that SHA (same-SHA attempt-level non-determinism, direct proof rather than a proxy: a deterministic failure cannot flip to passing on a byte-identical retry). Standard (b) never accepts same-SHA occurrences that are all 'failed' -- that is a deterministic failure and must never be registered. Plus a note establishing non-association with the observed slice. A new entry is C7 flake-classification scope -- routed to the delegate, never self-classified by the Supervisor.

testFile.description: Repo-relative test file path, matching the vitest JSON report's testResults[].name suffix.

testFullName.description: The failing assertion's full name (vitest's assertionResults[].fullName), the same identity generate-ledger.mjs's expectCases matching already uses.

outcome.description: Whether this specific CI attempt observed this test failing or passing. Required so scripts/first100/verify-flake-registry.ts can mechanically check the BLOCKED-023 same-SHA divergence standard (a 'passed' outcome is only ever recorded to prove non-determinism against a sibling 'failed' occurrence on the identical candidateSha -- never to pad the occurrence count).

absorbedByCell.description: The cell this absorption greened, as "<EPIC>.<STAGE>". Part of the append idempotency key together with ciRunUrl and candidateSha (generate-ledger.mjs:674-678): removing it lets a re-green of the same cell from the same run append a duplicate and inflate the rate this entry is judged by. Written on every new occurrence; absent on occurrences that predate that code, which is why it is not required.

verifiedBy.description: How this outcome was established, recorded at the moment of absorption. Written on every new occurrence; not required, for the same reason as absorbedByCell.

occurrences.description: Structural shape only (>=2 items) -- the real evidence-standard check (cross-SHA reproduction, or same-SHA outcome divergence) is BLOCKED-023, enforced by scripts/first100/verify-flake-registry.ts, not expressible as a pure JSON Schema constraint over this array.

unrelatedNote.description: Why this failure is not associated with the slices these CI runs actually observed -- e.g. distinct unrelated commits, or a commit touching zero product code.

registeredBy.description: Attribution for the classification decision, e.g. 'ANSWERED-BY-DELEGATE(gq-92)'.

notes.description: Hand-written prose about this entry. Nothing in scripts/ reads these; the grouping is what makes "prose or contract?" answerable by position.

timeoutNote.description: Why this entry is no longer read as non-determinism. A case whose cost sits inside its timeout fails and passes on one tree without being flaky; the occurrences stay, because they are what established that reading, and this says a later failure is a real regression rather than this flake.

candidate.description: A test seen failing but NOT registered. Its purpose is that a second occurrence is recognised as a second rather than a first, so it holds the evidence a future registration would be judged on. It is NOT an entry: it has never been registered, and it may carry a single occurrence. Promotion is a delegate act (C7), never expressed here.
